# Centennial Fountain Guide

> Independent visitor guide to Nicholas J. Melas Centennial Fountain in Chicago. Unaffiliated with MWRD or the City of Chicago.

Canonical website: https://centennialfountain.org/

## Visitor facts

- Location: River Esplanade Park, at N McClurg Court and E River Drive on the north bank of the Chicago River, Chicago, Illinois, USA.
- The water cannon is scheduled for 5 minutes at the top of each hour, 10 a.m. through 11 p.m., May 1–September 30, in Chicago time (America/Chicago).
- The countdown follows the published schedule, not live operating status. Weather and maintenance may interrupt the cannon.
- River Esplanade Park hours: 6 a.m.–11 p.m.; follow posted closures and leave by closing time.
- The fountain was dedicated in 1989; the Chicago River reversal occurred in 1900.
- Schedule verification date: 2026-11-15. Check MWRD for current operations.
- The game and maps are illustrative; the game does not control the real fountain.

## Pages

- [Centennial Fountain on the Chicago River](https://centennialfountain.org/): See Chicago’s river-spanning water cannon. Count down to the next firing, explore Centennial Fountain, and find your favorite riverfront viewpoint.
- [Visit Centennial Fountain — Schedule, Directions & Viewpoints](https://centennialfountain.org/visit/): Find your place to watch Centennial Fountain: north-bank plaza, south-bank Riverwalk, bridge views, water cannon schedule and walking directions.
- [Explore Centennial Fountain — Design, Details & History](https://centennialfountain.org/about/): Explore the sundial, stepped basins and water cannon. Meet architect Dirk Lohan and learn why Chicago dedicated the fountain in 1989.
- [Why Chicago Reversed Its River — An Interactive Guide](https://centennialfountain.org/river-reversal/): Switch between before and after 1900 to see how Chicago reversed its river to protect its drinking-water supply.
- [Play the Centennial Fountain Water Cannon Game](https://centennialfountain.org/play/): Fire the water cannon and splash passing boats in an endlessly looping Chicago River game.
